messages:
maya: quick follow-up from the RFC thread — we talked about splitting controlplane into a tiny in-customer 'observer' + central control. question: for customers that forbid inbound, should the agent be outbound-only TLS to our CP (single leaf cert) or should it do mutual TLS to a customer-managed peering endpoint? we need to nail egress semantics + ip preservation for logging/compliance.
arjun: outbound-only seems operationally simplest. agent opens TLS to our regional CP, we do client cert rotation. pros: no peering, simpler routing. cons: customer may want source-ip consistency for allowlists and audit logs.
sam: +1 for outbound-only but callout: if we NAT at a shared egress pool, customer will see a shared IP, which breaks per-tenant allowlists. options: per-tenant ephemeral elastic IPs, or source-preserving peering (but peering is heavy).
kelly: security/reg compliance: if we do client certs from our CA, customers ask who controls the CA and rotation. for high-compliance orgs they want either: 1) bring-your-own-ca + mTLS, or 2) validated egress IPs and long-lived cert pinning. both increase ops surface.
geoff: also think about fallback modes: if our regional CP is down, agent should be able to route to a relay in the same region (no inbound) or shift to a peered model as an emergency. that's a lot of complexity in the agent though.
maya: thinking tradeoffs: 1) outbound-only with ephemeral per-tenant egress IP allocation (best for customers that need per-tenant allowlist) 2) outbound-only shared IP + consent for shared egress (simpler) 3) customer-managed peering for strict network isolation. which is cheapest complexity-wise?
arjun: ranked by implementation effort: shared egress < ephemeral-per-tenant egress < peering. ephemeral IP allocation needs an address pool per-region + fast attach/detach flow. peering needs cross-account infra + routing and support for many customers.
sam: for ephemeral model we also need to ensure route table hygiene on attach/detach and fast propagation. suggestion: use a small controller that holds a /32 ENI per-tenant in a proxy VPC and map via source NATing. attach/detach ~10s with warm pool to avoid cold-start.
kelly: CA model: we can offer two knobs: redwood-managed CA (default) and customer-provided CA via a CSR flow + KMS-backed key material. record rotation policy in audit logs.
infra-bot: deploy: started ephemeral-egress-spike branch -> staging. link: https://ci.internal/1234 :rocket:
geoff: spike checklist: a) demo per-tenant egress attach/detach latency, b) verify source-ip seen by customer, c) perf impact of extra NAT hop, d) cert rotation handshake flow. keep it to a 3-day spike.
maya: tidy next steps: arjun + sam own the spike. kelly will draft the CA opt-in flow text for security review. I'll spin up a small RFC follow-up doc after spike. any objections?
arjun: ok from infra side, will PR a minimal agent flag `--egress-mode={shared,ephemeral,peered}` and add a simple config snippet for testing.
sam: I'll mock the attach/detach controller and a warm pool in staging.
maya: config snippet for the spike (short):

```
agent:
  egress:
    mode: ephemeral
    ip_pool: us-west-2-ephemeral
    tls:
      mode: mTLS
      ca: redwood-managed
      cert_rotation: 24h
```

maya: cool — if no one objects, i'll schedule the spike kickoff tomorrow at 10am PT. :thumbsup
thread_summary: Deciding outbound-only vs peering for private control-plane agent; tradeoffs: per-tenant ephemeral egress IPs, CA ownership, fallback relays; spike planned to test ephemeral attach/detach and cert rotation
